Hannah / team — see responses below (draft language & notes). I also attached a CSV for the supply/delivery timeline.

1) IP/ownership\- Draft response: Redwood does not seek assignment of customer-originated IP. Customer retains ownership of customer data, customer prompts, and any derivative models they develop using their data. Our order form includes a mutual license for Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry to improve service quality (see attached Redwood-IP-FAQ.pdf for standard language). For Atlas-specific SOW items (co-development), we can discuss a limited, time-bound license rather than assignment.

Suggested contract text (short):
"Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and Customer IP. Redwood is granted a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Aggregated De-Identified Data for the sole purpose of improving Redwood services and monitoring performance. Any co-developed deliverables will be addressed by a separate SOW that will specify ownership or licensing terms."

2) Indemnity & liability cap\- Draft response: Our baseline liability cap is the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form, or (ii) $1,000,000. We agree to carve-outs for breaches of confidentiality and willful misconduct (no cap). For data breach events tied to Redwood-controlled systems, we offer commitments aligned with our SOC 2 controls and are open to a mutually acceptable indemnity clause that references defined incident response SLAs.

Suggested contract text (short):
"Except for liability resulting from (i) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (ii) Redwood's breach of confidentiality obligations, the aggregate liability of either party arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event, or (b) $1,000,000."

If Atlas insists on a higher cap we can discuss escalators tied to committed spend tiers. Marissa — can you run scenarios for both the standard cap and a 3x-fees option and what discounts we would need to justify?

3) Supply/delivery schedule\- See attached Supply-Delivery-Schedule-2026Q3.csv. Summary: Dedicated capacity provisioning timeline is typically 6-8 weeks from signed PO for standard GPU pools; if Atlas requires pinned hardware or on-prem packaging that can extend to 10-12 weeks depending on region and procurement of customer-managed networking. Pilot deployments (shared capacity + config) can start within 2 weeks. We will include optional accelerated onboarding (paid) to shorten Dedicated provisioning to 3-4 weeks.

Attachments included: Redwood-IP-FAQ.pdf, Supply-Delivery-Schedule-2026Q3.csv, proposed redline PDF (ATLAS-OrderForm-Redline-v1.pdf).

Let me know if you want me to send this back to Atlas as-is or if Marissa/Laura want any commercial/legal tweaks first.

Thanks,
Aditya

Hi Sara / Atlas team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Please find attached a short Q&A PDF (answers for counsel), our redlined order form (changes we propose), and a delivery schedule CSV that maps pilot -> production milestones and estimated lead times. Summary of the key points below for quick reference:

- IP: Redwood does NOT require assignment of customer-originated IP. Customers retain ownership of data, prompts, and derivatives. We propose mutual language that allows Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvements, and a separate SOW for any co-development ownership details.

- Liability cap & indemnity: Baseline cap is the greater of 12 months' fees or $1,000,000. Carve-outs: confidentiality breaches and willful misconduct are uncapped. We are open to incident-specific indemnities tied to defined breach scenarios and our SOC 2 controls. If you need a higher cap, we can discuss escalators linked to committed spend.

- Delivery schedule: Pilot can begin within ~2 weeks of a signed LOA. Dedicated capacity (standard config) estimated 6-8 weeks; accelerated (paid) provisioning can reduce to ~3-4 weeks. On-prem/VPC options add coordination time (networking/KMS) — typically 10-12 weeks end-to-end.

Next steps: If Atlas Legal is comfortable with the attached Q&A and redline, please confirm and we will prepare a final Order Form for signature and a proposed LOA. If counsel prefers different wording on the cap or indemnity carve-outs, please send redlines and we'll route to legal for a fast turn.
